name: Village swaraj and the economy of permanence

thinkers.name: M. K. Gandhi
thinkers.note: The economics is scattered across forty years of journalism rather than gathered into a treatise, which is why it is so often summarised badly. Hind Swaraj in 1909 states the position; the Harijan columns of the 1930s and 1940s work out what it means for policy.

thinkers.name: J. C. Kumarappa
thinkers.note: The trained economist of the group, Columbia-educated, who turned Gandhi's positions into something with categories and a costing. Economy of Permanence, written in prison in 1945, is the closest the tradition has to a textbook.

claim: An economy should be organised around the village as a largely self-sufficient unit producing for local need with local labour, because centralised industrial production concentrates power, displaces the labour of a country that has labour to spare, and cannot be sustained by everyone.
summary: Hind Swaraj is not primarily about the British. Its argument is that modern industrial civilisation is itself the affliction, and that a free India running the same machinery from Delhi would have exchanged the rulers and kept the disease. Swaraj means rule over oneself before it means rule by Indians, and an economic arrangement is judged by whether it leaves people capable of that.

The unit is the village, and Gandhi's 1946 statement of it is precise: a complete republic, growing its own food and cotton, with its own school, its own sanitation, its own panchayat, dependent on neighbours for what it cannot make. He drew the picture as an oceanic circle of villages rather than a pyramid, in which the outer circle does not crush the inner but gives it strength.

Two arguments carry the economics. Machinery that displaces labour is destructive in a country whose surplus is labour, so the test of a technique is not output per worker but whether it employs the people who are there. Gandhi was clear that he was not against machinery as such, and pointed out that the spinning wheel is one. And wealth is held rather than owned: trusteeship asks the rich to administer their property for the society that produced it, which is the part of the programme that convinced almost nobody and which Gandhi defended anyway.

Kumarappa gave it the ecological formulation. An economy of permanence is one that lives on nature's income rather than its capital, and by that standard an industrial economy is not merely unjust but temporary. He asked in 1945 how many planets an industrialised world would need, which is the ecological footprint argument arriving about forty years early.

axis_notes.allocation: Neither state planning nor markets. Production for local use, coordinated by the village itself, with the state pushed down rather than expanded.
axis_notes.priority: Sufficiency rather than growth. The last person is the test, which Gandhi put as a talisman rather than a metric.
axis_notes.hierarchy: The hardest to place and the most contested. Gandhi campaigned against untouchability for decades and defended varna as an ideal of duty for much of his life, moving late and incompletely. Ambedkar's charge is that the second position undermined the first.
axis_notes.agency: Villagers, constructive workers and the moral conversion of the powerful. Not planners, and not a state acting on society from above.

layers.title: The diagnosis is civilisation, not colonialism
layers.text: Hind Swaraj argues that a machine civilisation multiplies wants, concentrates power in whoever controls the machinery, and makes people dependent on arrangements they cannot see or control. Independence that keeps the arrangement swaps the operator. This is why Gandhi's economics cannot be detached from his politics: they are answers to the same question.

layers.title: India's abundant factor is people
layers.text: A technique that raises output per worker while shedding workers is progress where labour is scarce and destruction where it is not. Gandhi's objection to the textile mill is not aesthetic; it is that the mill produces cloth a village could produce, using capital a village does not have, and removes the winter employment of people who have no other. The charkha is a technology choice, argued on those grounds.

layers.title: So production should sit where consumption is
layers.text: Swadeshi in its strict sense: use what your neighbourhood produces, and produce what your neighbourhood uses. Food and cloth first, then the rest. The village is not self-sufficient out of nostalgia but because a short circuit between producing and consuming is what keeps control local and keeps the surplus from travelling.

layers.title: Which makes the village the political unit
layers.text: A village that feeds and clothes itself can govern itself, and Gandhi's panchayat has legislative, judicial and executive functions together, elected annually by adults. Power flows outward from it rather than downward to it. The image he chose against the pyramid was an oceanic circle: the outermost ring gives strength to the inner rings and takes its own strength from them.

layers.title: Property is held, not owned
layers.text: Trusteeship. Someone with more than they need administers the excess on behalf of society, voluntarily, and is entitled to a reasonable return for the work of administering it. Gandhi preferred this to expropriation because a state that can take property is a state powerful enough to be worth capturing. Almost nobody accepted the argument, including many of his own followers, and he continued to make it.

layers.title: An economy that can last
layers.text: Kumarappa's addition, and the one that has aged best. An economy of permanence takes from nature only what nature replaces, and by that test an industrial order is borrowing rather than earning. He asked how the planet would supply an industrialised world at British consumption levels, and treated the answer as decisive. Sarvodaya, the welfare of all, is the endpoint: judged by the last person, not by an average.

evidence.finding: It was, though not in the form proposed. The 73rd Amendment in 1992 made three-tier panchayats mandatory with regular elections and reserved seats, producing roughly a quarter of a million panchayats and around three million elected representatives, a third of them women by law and more than that in states which went further. What was withheld is money and staff: devolution of the subjects listed in the Eleventh Schedule has been partial in most states, so the institution exists with a fraction of the powers.
evidence.source: Ministry of Panchayati Raj; Constitution (Seventy-third Amendment) Act 1992 and the Eleventh Schedule

evidence.claim: Local control produces decisions closer to local need.
evidence.finding: Supported where it has been tested properly. Raghabendra Chattopadhyay and Esther Duflo used the random assignment of women-reserved pradhan seats in West Bengal and Rajasthan and found that reserved panchayats invested more in the goods women in those states named as priorities, drinking water in West Bengal and roads in Rajasthan. Kerala's People's Plan Campaign from 1996, which moved a large share of state plan funds to local bodies, is the strongest Indian case that the devolution can be made real rather than formal.
evidence.source: Chattopadhyay and Duflo, Econometrica; Kerala State Planning Board

evidence.claim: The village is a suitable unit for the people at the bottom of it.
evidence.finding: This is where the theory takes its heaviest damage, and the criticism is Ambedkar's rather than a later economist's. A unit in which land, credit and employment are held along caste lines does not become fair by being made autonomous, and the persistence of untouchability practice reported by around a quarter of households in national survey data is measured in villages that now have elected panchayats.
evidence.source: India Human Development Survey; Ambedkar's Constituent Assembly speech of 4 November 1948

evidence.claim: Village industry can hold employment against factory production.
evidence.finding: Only where it was protected, and the protection had costs. The Khadi and Village Industries Commission has supported village industry continuously since 1956 and khadi remains a live sector, but the reservation of products for small-scale industry, which was the policy instrument, kept firms below the size at which they could invest and was progressively dismantled after 1991 for that reason.
evidence.source: Khadi and Village Industries Commission; Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises de-reservation record

unsettled: The employment argument and the ecological argument have separated, and each is now doing better than the tradition that carried them both. Choosing techniques by how many people they employ is being argued again under other names, and Kumarappa's question about what an industrialised world would take from the planet is now a discipline with journals. What has not survived is the claim that the village is the right container for either, and Ambedkar's objection is the reason. Whether a Gandhian economics can be detached from the village and still be Gandhian is a real question, and Schumacher's answer in 1973, that it can, is the one most people since have taken.
india: Every argument about Indian development runs into this one eventually, usually through the 73rd Amendment, through the debate about labour-intensive against capital-intensive industry, or through the environmental movement. Its opponents in the Constituent Assembly won: the Indian constitution is centralised, the village appears in the Directive Principles rather than in the operative articles, and Nehru told Gandhi plainly in October 1945 that he did not accept the picture. That the panchayat was written back in half a century later, and then not funded, is the shape the argument has taken since.
compare_note: Kumarappa's permanence and the Chipko argument about who the forest is for are the same claim about who bears the cost of extraction.
contrast_note: The central quarrel in modern Indian thought. One reads the village as a republic, the other as the machinery of caste with a wall around it.
